newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - BNP may signal revival for French banks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - BNP may signal revival for French banks.

text.p: Banque Nationale de Paris offered the first signs of turnaround for beleaguered French banks when it kicked off the results reporting season on Thursday with the announcement of an 80 percent rise in first-half profits.

Chairman Michel Pebereau said banking income had bucked the trend of the last two years with a increase in the first six months of the year and that he expected revenues to stay on the rise in the second half of 1996.

BNP, one of the "Big Three" mainstream banks, beat analysts' expectations to report a net attributable profit of 1.74 billion francs ($339 million), versus a profit of 966 million in the same period last year.

Net banking income rose 4.8 percent to 19.22 billion francs, a figure which analysts said showed a welcome turnaround even if this was still well below those in places like Britain, Germany or Switzerland and it was too early to read too much into it.
BNP shares rose on the news, up 2.16 percent at 193.6 francs at 1145 GMT, while CCF stock was also up. Other bank stocks also firmed, with Societe Generale up 1.39 percent at 584.
"BNP is back to a level of profitability which is still not satisfactory in our view but it's a step," Pebereau told a news conference.

All operations had done better and the growth was all the more significant given the "hesitant" growth of the economy and tough competition exacerbated by thin margins due to persistent distortions in the French banking sector, BNP said.

"The rise in receipts generated by banking activities in France confirms the reversal of a trend we have observed since the second quarter of 1995 and makes clear the growing commercial efficiency of the BNP's domestic banking network," it said in a statement.
Immediate reactions from analysts were positive, both for banks reporting results on Thursday and on the implications for French banks generally.

"It's a very good result," said Jime Hyde, banking analyst at stockbrokers Williams de Broe in London, adding that he had upgraded his BNP profit forecasts for this year and those of CCF bank for next year after good results from the latter as well.
"It's the same basic picture as CCF (bank), there's also talk of a recovery retail banking recovery," Hyde said on BNP.

Credit Commercial de France (CCF) reported a rise in net attributable profit to 668.8 million francs from 596 million and also reported a 6.7 percent rise in net banking income to 4.81 billion francs.
Brian Crossley, analyst at broker ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett, said the results were promising for the sector but cautioned that the depressed lending climate was still a point of concern.
Pebereau declined to make predictions on profit for 1996.
On a more sobre note for French banking generally, Pebereau warned that BNP would not stand idle if others continued to cut prices in a depressed lending market.

He said BNP had been an "exemplary pupil" in respecting the repeated calls by Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet for banks to steer clear of cut-throat competition on loan interest rates, but that he would be forced to act if others ignored the advice.
Bank lending levels had slipped further this year, notably corporate lending, and margins were still under pressure. BNP lending slipped 2.2 percent, but deposits rose 9.1 percent.

BNP made lower provisions this time round for doubtful loans and exposure to a property market which has taken a heavy toll on banks in recent years after their investments turned sour with the collapse of property prices in the early 1990s.
Net new provisions dropped to 2.46 billion francs from 2.82 billion, the bank said in a statement.
